3 Breaded onion, potato cakes, and avocado salad

4 Veggie balls (no meat), mushroom sauce, and polenta

5 Toasted tomato parcels, sweet peppers, zucchini, and asparagus

6 Very spicy ratatouille (hot!)

1d6 Smoking Cat Dessert of the day 1 Apple pie with almonds 2 Melon and mint sorbet 3 Apple sauce with bits of biscuits 4 Hot chocolate with cinnamon 5 Banana chocolate muffin 6 Blueberry and fig crumble

pages.name: p.98 - Old Man Chompy’s Workshop
pages.html:
Ignatius Ignatius is a nice but always busy restaurateur. A demanding perfect- ionist, he is always accommodating, and is one of the most popular people in the neighborhood. Walter has asked him several times to become his official chef, but he always refuses to leave his neighborhood. Ignatius knows the location of the kingdom's meowgic vending machines and regularly stocks up on chocolate bars, sweets, and bags of colorful candy. He puts them into large colored metal boxes and lets Kittens use them freely. He may reveal the location of some of them to Kittens in exile, allowing them to easily find food, if they are nice and polite. But they should be careful not to use them too much.

Strong 2 / Smart 3 / Cute 3 // Heart points 5 // Cook; Make Music // Clean & Tidy (1); Preserving Resources (1) // A recipe book; a guide to edible mushrooms; a hand- drawn map of meowgic vending machines.

Old Man Chompy’s Workshop

Since Walter launched his industrialization program in the capital, large factories and massive manufacturing plants have replaced the myriad of small workshops that occupied the ground floors of houses and courtyards in the neighborhood. There are still a few, however, and perhaps the most famous of all is owned by Old Man Chompy. Right from the start, he resisted pressure from King Walter to close his workshop, so his house could be knocked down and a new factory built in its place. He is in possession of some old property deeds that mean the king cannot do as he wishes. But Old Man Chompy has paid the price for his stubbornness: three grandsons and two granddaughters were exiled and now it is a very sad house indeed. Still Old Man Chompy keeps working, making useful and beautiful objects, repairing the old things that people bring him. He also takes on apprentices—with the constant risk that they may be exiled—but people in the neighborhood will take this risk. And bit by bit, Old Man Chompy has become perhaps the most important figure in the resistance against Walter. Neighbors take turns to keep an eye on the premises and avoid vandalism and “accidental” fires.

pages.name: p.99
pages.html:
Old Man Chompy A quiet and stubborn cat, Old Man Chompy hates Walter and everything he stands for; he detests the nobility and does all he can to annoy the Royal Guard. An anarchist and libertarian, he loathes everything that even remotely looks like an authority symbol. And in spite of himself, he has become a symbol of the resistance against Walter—he certainly did not want to become a leader or a revolutionary. On the other hand, he did develop a taste for political thought, and found some ancient human books on the subject. He teaches the more willing young cats about political ethics and morals so that they can be ready to organize things when Walter’s reign is over.

Strong 4 / Smart 4 / Cute 2 // Heart points 8 // Keep Calm & Carry On; Move Silently; Tinker with Bits & Bobs// Leather

Apron (1); Safety at Work (1); Summon

Tools (2) // A battered old leather tool bag; a small book of anarchist sayings; an ancient multimeter.

Crusty Crusty is a one-eyed old tomcat who is a few grains short of a bowl of kittysnacks. He lives as a beggar in the Soot District. He always wants to help, but never manages to do anything. He is not mean, just a bit clingy. And when he daydreams, his head wobbling like a toy, he occasionally talks about his nephew who forced him from the throne… Crusty is in fact a fallen monarch, who is a bit lonely since his subjects have long forgotten him.

Strong 2 / Smart 3 / Cute 3 // Heart points 5 // Knowledge of Laws & Legends; Knowledge of People & Places // Fearless (1); Sense Trouble (3) // An old floppy hat.

pages.name: p.101 - The Sewers
pages.html:
The Sewers

Beneath Cat Tree City and its suburbs, underground, there are galleries, tunnels, pipes, reservoirs, walkways, corridors, and passageways that form what the locals call “The Sewers”. This is where all the city’s wastewater flows, before disappearing into the unfathomable depths. In fact, the sewers are a tiny piece of the city that stretches out, invisible, underneath it (see page 121).

The Pillow Knights

street gang Not all exiled Kittens leave Cat Tree City. Under the leadership of a street Kitten who knew his way around the sewers, a small group pretended to leave one day, but then came back and hid here. They live where it's warm, in a series of small, comfortable, and well-equipped rooms, with piles of toys, thick blankets, and books that they have “borrowed” from the library. For food, they go to the bridge and collect what the peasants throw or give away, or maybe make a tour of the backrooms of Chopton. These little Kittens are quite a handful.

Matey Mousetail

Matey is a skinny Kitten, with a mostly hairless tail that makes him look like a big mouse—hence his nickname. A street Kitten condemned to exile, he had no intention of leaving Cat Tree City to wander penniless in the wilds of the country. He dragged some other exiles with him, as well as a few of his gang members, to found their own refuge under the city. Lazy and mischievous, Matey is an organiser but he does not do much: He eats, plays, sleeps, reads a lot, and then sleeps some more. However, he knows all the alleys and secret passageways that lead to the top of the tower.

Strong 2 / Smart 2 / Cute 4 // Heart points 4 // Read, Write, Count; Seduce & Charm // Hide Things (2); Leave no Trace (1) // A wall-colored cape; map of all the floors of Cat Tree City.

pages.name: p.102
pages.html:
The Ballroom Just below the Soot District, there is a huge, round, vaulted room, with perfect acoustics, completely isolated from the surface. It was there that Bruno, a mild-mannered and charming cat, one day found a strange machine: A barrel organ and its entire collection of music. At first just a few cats and Kittens would come down to dance to the sounds coming from the machine, like a private club. But word soon got out and more and more people turned up. However, Bruno was anxious not to attract Walter’s attention, so he ended up making a whole mechanism of sliding walls and secret doors that transformed the way into the place into a maze, which changes every week. Only the inhabitants of the Soot District know about the changes and no nobles from the tower have ever made it inside.

Bruno Bruno is a lovely looking cat with a silky coat, bright eyes, and a charming smile. He knows it and he takes advantage of it. He is also a fine musician who can play many instruments well. His great stroke of luck, that occurred while he was barely getting by with his music, was to find the ballroom and the barrel organ. He plays old tunes that he found in the boxes with the machine. Maybe they were tunes that the big-bare-butts danced to, long ago. But for some time now, he has been adding some new tunes to the collection: his own songs that he learned to program with holes in cardboard. The new tunes have gone down really well, although no one knows that he is the one who wrote them.

Strong 1 / Smart 2 / Cute 5 // Heart points 3 // Make Music; Seduce & Charm // Enchanting Voice (2); Loud Speaker (1); Sound & Vision (1) // A shamisen; a barrel organ; Brylcreem to slick down his hair.

pages.name: p.103 - The Wastelands
pages.html:
The albino crocodile No sewer tour would be complete without a mention of the great albino crocodile that lives down there. So here goes... That’s pretty much all that’s known about it!

Strong 5 / Smart 2 / Cute 1 // Heart points 7 // Scratch // Very big teeth.

The Wastelands

Outside of the suburbs are the Wastelands, some small, sparse woodland, and aban doned plots of land. It is the perfect place if you want to build a hut and play hide-and-go-seek, but it is not without danger: Holes can open up at any time to drag the unfortunate underground; horrible creatures live there; Yardogs sometimes venture there to keep watch on the city and are happy to leave with a prisoner or two. Nevertheless, it makes for a nice playground for adventurous Kittens.

Cockroaches More of a nuisance than a danger, waste land cockroaches are huge, crawling insects the size of a large tortoise. They are not particularly aggressive and even a bit fearful, but they leave an awful stench and a foul trail behind them.

The countryside

As far as the eye can see, beyond the city walls, are the rolling hills of the countryside, with fields and pastures that are carefully maintained by generations of peasants. Far from the vertical, cramped surroundings of Cat Tree City, country Kittens dwell in the open air, surrounded by flourishing fields. However, their distance from the capital makes them much more vulnerable to interference from the Yardogs.

Tina the traveller Tina never learned how to fly and has suffered a lot. She hides the fact that she’s a bird under a large cape with a hood. She follows Kittens all over, to have stories to tell her family when they are back from migrating. She’s a bit clingy and maybe even annoying, but it’s mainly because she is lonely.

Strong 3 / Smart 4 / Cute 4 // Heart points 7 // Find Your Way; Hunter-Gatherer; Read Sky & Stars // Leave no Trace (1); Quick as a Flash (2) // A large, hooded cape; small Purr-ecious items in a designer handbag.

entries.name: Elsewhere in the Kingdom of Cats

pages.name: p.105 - Elsewhere in the Kingdom
pages.html:
Elsewhere in the Kingdom

of Cats

All around the imposing Cat Tree City there are many remarkable places that are the settings for the Kittens’ first adventures.

pages.name: p.106 - Highcastle School
pages.html:
Highcastle School

The kingdom’s school of meowgic is built in an old water tower southwest of Cat Tree City. It is undoubtedly the most impressive place in the region, after Cat Tree City itself. The water in the big cistern was enchanted by the meowges. In turn, this has transformed the local plant life into a wonderful, vibrant jungle.

Unfortunately, this little paradise still falls under

Walter's jurisdiction and its inhabitants still have to bow to the king, although it is said that its

principal, the great archmeowge Milena,

is not a particularly loyal subject.

Adventure trails Lately, the Yardogs have been using the area around Highcastle as a garbage dump. Noxious, fluorescent liquids have mixed with meowgic water to turn the plants into strange carnivorous creatures

(see The Junkyard, page 125).

Milena has disappeared and was last seen heading to the Slumbering Forest (see page 131) in order to appease Selene, the spirit of the forest. Is she lost in one of the guardian’s nightmares?

Paintings at Highcastle hint at the story of the

Dreamsinger, an amazing instrument that’s currently owned by an eccentric amusement park manager (see page 155).

pages.name: p.107 - Count Catula’s
pages.html:
Count Catula’s

Manorhouse

A wizened old tomcat with a wobbly chin and two big teeth moved into an old, creaking house northeast of Cat Tree City. It is said that he is so old he may be immortal. Count Catula is a mysterious individual who suffers from a strange disease (see Hooting Kittens, page 29).

No one knows if he is actually an eccentric pretending, a real Hooting Kitten or something even more terrifying. Whatever the case, he looks after the few Hooting Kittens of the kingdom, who have nowhere else to go.

He is like a father to the many Kittens who have moved into the old creaking shack of a house, where they sleep during the day—safely away from the burning rays of the sun—and party at night.

Unfortunately, the Royal Guard will always be able to find a Kitten to send him into exile if Walter asks, even ones tucked away in this mansion that’s far away from everything.

pages.name: p.108
pages.html:
Count Catula This cat with two big canine teeth—the last two he has left—only comes out at night, dressed in a strange suit, to feast on red, sweet berries. He has frightened many nightstrollers and illicit lovers by suddenly appearing from behind a bush, his face blood red with berry goo. Walter is scared of Count Catula and will not provoke him without good reason. However, Catula always obeys the law, and never complains or causes a fuss.

Strong 2 / Smart 5 / Cute 5 // Heart points 7 // Keep Calm & Carry On; Knowledge of Laws & Legends; Make Music; Move Silently // Animate Object (3); Endless Feed (2); Long Night (3); Quick as a Flash (2) // An odd purple suit; a large night cape; an ultraviolet lamp; a suitcase with wheels.

Adventure trails Count Catula is wrongly accused of kidnapping a Kitten. It is actually one of the Yardogs’ dirty tricks (see page 125). He needs to be rapidly released and the real culprits found before the villagers get out the burning torches and pitchforks! Count Catula has to leave the kingdom for a while to go on a journey with his protégé. He asks the kittens to look after the manor while he is away… And goodness me, that old place of his is scary at night! Count Catula has invited his neighbors to his mega birthday party (two hundred years—definitely a big one!) But no one has replied to his invitations… Could the Kittens possibly convince the villagers of

Catula’s good intentions? And what’s more, what are they planning as a gift?

pages.name: p.110 - The Caravan Village
pages.html:
The Caravan Village

To the north of Cat Tree City is a self-governing community made up of old caravans that are all powered by meowgic. Merchants and wandering artists—all highly regarded in Corktown (see page 143)— live in the caravans. However, Walter does not think much of all this freedom. He has started some nasty rumors about these nomads, accusing them of various horrible things. Any Kittens who make it to the caravan village will encounter nothing but nice, friendly cats. And although they seem not to care, the group has a deep-seated fear of

Walter’s reprisals. That’s why the inhabitants are always ready to move on at a moment’s notice.

pages.name: p.111 - Mama, the village
pages.html:
Mama, the village

matriarch

Mama is an old shaggy-haired cat with colorful fur. Her exact age is unknown, but it is said that she knew Walter when he was just a Kitten. She is usually dressed in a long, baggy robe with hundreds of metallic jewels that jingle at every step. She moves and speaks slowly, but nothing seems to alter her willingness to fight the nasty King Walter.

Strong 1 / Smart 5 / Cute 4 // Heart points 6 // Herbology; Heal Wounds & Diseases; Knowledge of Laws & Legends; Knowledge of People & Places; Sweet-talk; Find Your Way // Care (3); Feel the Path (3); Treating Beasts (1) // Long, colorful scarves; medallions around her neck; a large, carved walking stick.

Adventure trails

Walter has arranged for a delivery of sweet baked goods intended for Kittens in the suburbs of Cat Tree City to be hijacked, and blamed on the caravan owners. Royal Guards have been sent to the village and they are determined to find evidence of theft, even if they have to make it themselves.

Mama, the matriarch, knows Suzanne, the seer of the marshes (see page 137) as she asked her for advice a long time ago. In exchange for a spectacular show, she will give the Kittens what they need to pay the viper for a vision. The Kittens arrive just as the caravans are leaving. If they ask nicely, they may be able to hitch a ride on one of the carriages headed for Corktown (see page 143), unless they would rather go to Bigwheel (see page 155). In either case, with the Yardogs lurking (see page 125), their journey will not be a restful one.

pages.name: p.112 - Catnut Swamp
pages.html:
Catnut Swamp

West of Cat Tree City, in a swampy rain forest, live some very strange creatures: Catnuts. These hairy cats are, for the most part, exiled Kittens who decided to cut all ties with the Kingdom of Cats and settled in the woods to live like hermits. They have little contact with each other and even less with the outside world—it is impossible to know how many of them there are.

All kinds of legends circulate about them, but it is difficult to know what is real, as Catnuts are difficult to find in the forest they know so well. They can effortlessly hide and move around concealed in plain sight. Not to mention their natural ability to never actually look like the hairy cats that are sought.

They have developed a sort of natural armor that covers their hair, making them look like big chestnuts. This armor, combined with their mud-matted and leaf-tangled fur, means Catnuts are the perfect bogeyman for scary fireside stories.

“If you never take a bath, the Catnuts will drag you down into the swamp!”

pages.name: p.113
pages.html:
It is true that Catnuts are frightening, but it is because they are introverted and painfully shy that they have this reputation. If a Kitten proves themselves trustworthy, a Catnut will make for a friendly host and a loyal friend.

Chuck the Catnut Chuck is an impressive, burly Kitten who is covered in dried mud, leaves, branches, and probably more besides. He grew up in the marshes and knows nothing about the civilized world of Cat Tree City. He is uncomfortable if he is surrounded by walls or if there are more people than he can count (and that’s not many). Silent and lonely, his talents are revealed deep in the forest, where he has no fear, where he always finds something to eat (but you will need a stomach of iron to share one of his feasts), and where he moves around the branches faster than a squirrel. And he’s a friend you can always count on!

Strong 5 / Smart 2 / Cute 3 // Heart points 7 // Hiss & Growl; Hunter-Gatherer; Shake Your Booty // Earthworks (1); Slice and Dice (1) // A large whip to wrap around branches and swing away; chestnut throwing bugs.

Adventure trails A Catnut is trapped in a fire caused by lightning. He is totally panicked and it will be necessary to calm him down to help him. The villagers in the area talk about a scary creature from the marshes that is sometimes seen at the edge of the woods, but it is probably a Catnut in need of a good bath. Walter considers the marsh a thorn in his side, right in the middle of his beautiful kingdom. He becomes fixated on it. Sooner or later, he will want to have it drained, no matter who lives there.

pages.name: p.115 - The port village of
pages.html:
The port village of

Huggle

To the northeast of Cat Tree City is a small seaside village named Huggle. It is where all the salt beer in Cat Tree City comes from. Its inhabitants have developed an entire brewing technique that takes advantage of the sea’s tidal movements: The village’s lightly salted but highly refreshing beers and lemonades are known and loved throughout the kingdom, right up to the highest floors of Cat Tree City.

The village also has a small port from which you can set sail for Corktown (see page 143)—the kingdom’s biggest consumer of salt beer! Some Kittens also set off from Huggle to join a quest for treasure in dangerous places, such as Crimsonfief (see page 247).

Captain Buttercup Buttercup loves the sea, ships, sailors' shanties, and seafood! She became captain of her ship, Summer Solstice, after she won it in a game of chance. Some claim that she must have used loaded dice, but nobody would dare to say that to her face. Buttercup is a headstrong woman who leads her crew masterfully. She is a fierce and fearsome duelist, a lover and a fighter—and a swashbuckling adventuress. Do you have a dangerous mission? A lost cause? An unexplored region to visit? Pirates to chase? Captain Buttercup will rent you her services with pleasure!

Strong 3 / Smart 4 / Cute 3 // Heart points 7 // Find Information; Hiss & Growl; Knowledge of People & Places; Read Sky & Stars // Balancing Cat (2); Breathe Under Water (1); Feel the Path (3) // A map of the coast of the kingdom and beyond; a spyglass.

Adventure trails A strange rumor tells of a luminous

Kittenfish that comes out of the water at dusk. A group of Yardogs have built a makeshift submarine to get into the caves of Huggle so they can steal the precious beer. A gigantic blue whale ran aground on Huggle’s reef. A group of sailors is desperately trying to get her back into the sea.

pages.name: p.116 - The Great Pyramid
pages.html:
The Great Pyramid

To the south of the Kingdom of Cats is a strange glass pyramid surrounded by a stretch of burnt, red sand. Some travelers say that a powerful meowge reduced everything in this land to dust, apart from this transparent creation.

The hollow building conceals a maze of underground passages and corridors that contain fabulous treasure. Much of the present fortune of the Kingdom of Cats has come from the trade in the statues and jewels that Walter’s minions have been digging out over a number of years—until they awakened something.

For many generations, cats have feared and respected this unique place—until Walter’s greed led him to desecrate it. And Walter‘s plunderers were not alone, his greed attracted other explorers and adventurers, until strange rumors about mummified creatures walking around deep beneath the pyramid began to circulate.

These undead Kittens are called Meowmies (see page 30). There are not very many of them, and most remain in the shelter of the pyramid. Sometimes, however, a Meowmy leaves their cozy sarcophagus far beneath the ground and goes out to make friends.

pages.name: p.117
pages.html:
Mimi the Meowmy Mimi is a Meowmy who has only just left the pyramid. This is the first time her bandages have seen the light of day. She was woken up only a few days ago by looters sent by Walter. She has been wandering around ever since. She has decided to gather up as many stolen artifacts as possible and bring them back safely to the pyramid.

Strong 2 / Smart 2 / Cute 2 // Heart points 4 // Pickpocket; Move Silently // Enchanting Voice (2); Preserving Resources (1) // An ancient mirror; potent fragrances; a strange headdress with snakes on it; a large backpack of bandages that can hold as much as you put in it.

Adventure trails Meowmies do not like to to have their rest disturbed. However, since Walter started on his expansion of the Kingdom of Cats, strange machines have been unearthing the fields and disturbing all the way down to the depths of the crypt. There is no way to sleep peacefully. Can the Kittens find a solution to calm the anger of the ancient ones? The Meowmies do not have much to occupy their time. And although they are a little scary, they have very little to do. Maybe the Kittens could put on a show or take their favorite board games down there? A jackal-headed stone creature named

Anubis wanders the surface of the kingdom. It was removed from the pyramid while still in the form of a statue, but now seeks to return to the Meowmies it once protected.

pages.name: p.118 - The Jammed Radio Tower
pages.html:
The Jammed Radio Tower

From up in the heights of Cat Tree City, you can see an old metal tower far away on a hill to the north. It has a flashing light and, sometimes, a strange sound comes from it too. In the taverns it is said that on the top of the tower is a meowgic artifact, the “Chatter Box”.

However, before getting their paws on this fabulous object, it's a long way to the tower and a perilous climb to the top for the Kittens!

Adventure trails One Kitten has a recurring dream in which curious music draws him to the tower, a strange place on the top of a steep hill. Walter has heard of the Chatter Box and he wants to get his hands on it, but he won’t send his guard because it’s such a risky journey. But the Kittens could volunteer. The Kittens spot a group of Bojosar’s bully toads (see page 137). They overhear the toads boasting about their plans to invade the kingdom. Our heroes cannot stand by and do nothing!

The Chatter Box

The Chatter Box is a mysterious artifact. When the Kittens find it for the first time, the storyteller secretly rolls 1d6, or chooses a power from the list below. With a little time and work, Kittens will be able to unlock more powers.

1. The box amplifies a voice in a surprising way.

2. The box can record a sound or speech and reproduce it at will. 3. The box can create a soundwave that knocks large things over and shatters small objects.

4. The box emits mesmerizing music that forces creatures to dance. 5. The box receives strange broadcasts, containing random pieces of information. 6. The box unfolds to reveal a talking robot. Nice: a new companion

pages.name: p.121 - Even further away
pages.html:
Even further away

Downtown

Downtown is the name that animals have given to the still-standing remains of the kingdom of the big-bare-butts: Scattered all around are concrete and steel buildings, stretches of road, and industrial complexes rusting in the rain… Animals do go

Downtown, but they rarely stay. It is unpleasant and most of it is tarmacked over. In short, it is nasty and it makes creatures feel uneasy. In all the places you can get in and out of

Downtown there are tunnels that lead down to obscure, hidden depths these are called the

GIN (Great Inter-

raccoon Network).

This is where you’ll find the Kingdom of Rats. Unknown to the cats of the kingdom, it sprawls out over a huge distance (even as far as the sewers of Cat Tree City, see page 101). And, for a favour or a small payment, rats will guide the Kittens from one place to another using the tunnels and the machines that run in them. There are old repaired subway trains here: without being seen by the Yardogs, it is possible to travel in trains from Crimsonfief to Cat Tree City, from Huggle to Corktown, or as far as Bigwheel.

For the Storyteller and players alike, this is an opportunity to set a scene somewhere they may know or be familiar with—a small, rural village, or a futuristic-brutalist city neighborhood.

pages.name: p.122
pages.html:
1d6 What can be found Downtown… 1 A stadium with a dug-up pitch and deflated balls. 2 An airplane cabin half sunk in a swimming pool. 3 A glass-and-steel shopping mall filled with big, rotten things. 4 A cinema still showing a film on a stained screen. 5 A creepy subway station with a restaurant run by rats. 6 An old zoo—funnily enough, most animals avoid it...

1d6 On a street corner, you could meet… 1 A patrol of foraging rats with headlamps. 2 A magnificent deer with flowers growing on its antlers, crossing the street. 3 A small group of merchant ferrets pushing a shopping cart. 4 Carrier pigeons stopped to share the latest gossip. 5 A group of animals taking a break in a disused laundromat. 6 A rat musician playing all sorts of instruments in a music shop.

1d6 The GIN has some interesting options... 1 A boat made of old jam jars, floating in the drains.

2 A small mechanical car on the rusty rails of an old subway line. It’s practical but it sure is squeaky!

3 A narrow path through a mine or a burrow. There are shiny stones everywhere!

4 Chuckie, a giant centipede who was tamed by the rats, winds his way through the tunnels.

5 A homemade submarine built by a clever rat. Let’s explore the water table!

6 A supernatural toilet flush that teleports the traveler to the destination they are thinking of… Makes a big splash!

pages.name: p.123
pages.html:
The Kingdom of Rats The ruins of human cities frighten most animals. They are haunted by unpleasant memories and are still polluted—very little grows through the gray concrete and certainly nothing you could eat.

The streets are silent, occasionally disturbed by the echo of deer hooves on the road. Still wild, the deer flee at the slightest sound and disappear into the foliage of a town square-turned-forest. Night falls and yet, as if by magic, some of the neon signs suddenly start to crackle, then light up, making this empty place feel like an abandoned fairground.

This is thanks to the rats. They were already around when the big-bare-butts were alive, and they learned a lot from watching them. And ever since, they have kept going as best they could with what the humans left behind.

Rats consider the big-bare-butts to be demigods: immense and powerful; creatures to be feared. Beings who ensured the wealth and survival of their race. Since their disappearance, the lives of rats has got much harder and more complicated. This is why some rats pray every night for the return of humans.

Beep and Squeek, sewer archaeologists These two rats have a distinct look. They have headlamps on their helmets, large backpacks, and tools for exploring. They are brilliant engineers and can make just about anything with the things they find. They roam relentlessly beneath Downtown and know how to make their way around better than absolutely anyone else down there.

Strong 2 / Smart 3 / Cute 3 // Heart points 5 // Find Your Way; See & Search // Headlamp; pickaxe and rope; reel of twine; mechanic's kit.

Louis the Learned Louis is an ancient wise man who sits on top of an old television set. He produces plays which animals act out in his broken TV. All the plays are about the olden days, humans, catastrophe, as well as love, and some thrilling adventures. All the animals in the area love to come along to the performances.

Strong 1 / Smart 5 / Cute 4 // Heart points 6 // Knowledge of Laws & Legends;

Sweet-talk // An old book about the theater; a (disconnected) microphone; some VHS videocassettes.

pages.name: p.125 - The Junkyard
pages.html:
The Junkyard

Dogs were once man’s best friends, but these days they are on their own. Wanderers, hermits, mystics—dogs hang around simply hoping for the return of their masters, the only ones who can bring meaning back to their lives. Unfortunately, some dogs have given in to this melancholy mood and are bitter and violent. For them, there are no sunny future to look forward to, only a life of crime in the Junkyard.

The Junkyard is not a very nice place, even for the dogs that live there. It’s little more than a large, open-air dump, where old rusty cars are piled next to barrels of stinking molasses and rotten, broken sofas. And sinister black smoke constantly, winds skywards from the smouldering tire fire. It is visible from miles away, marking the location of the Yardogs’ stronghold.

The daily life of a Yardog consists of beating metal objects into crude but effective weapons or rusty, misshapen armor.

After a morning of hard work, Yardogs prowl in a pack, patrolling the surrounding areas in the hope they can loot some stuff or kidnap animals to work in their place while they wait for a ransom. Whether they’re out on foot or riding in one of their noisy, souped-up jalopies, the Yardogs are always noticed and feared wherever they go. And when night falls, crazy crescendos of barking and wild howling—mean yet sad at the same time—can be heard.

For any animal unlucky enough to be forced to work in the Junkyard, that will only be the start of their problems. Every day they will work their paws to the bone for their captors before they collapse, exhausted, in one of the containers that serve as crude dorms. However, it is not impossible to escape from here, and some prisoners have noticed that the pack of dogs are not a completely united group. Many downtrodden workers are waiting for the right moment to flee, and the arrival of the Kittens will undoubtedly help.

pages.name: p.126 - Brutus: The Leader
pages.html:
Brutus: The Leader

of the Pack Brutus is the first leader of the gang who is not just a dumb dog. He’s a small, somewhat ridiculous pug, but he is devilishly clever. Mean and petty, he managed to become leader by playing the other, tougher contenders against each other. Since then, he has introduced strict discipline and vastly increased the production of weapons and armor. As a consequence, Yardog raids are better prepared, more frightening, and bolder than ever.

He thinks dogs should stop living like nomads and claim the lands of the Kingdom of Cats, but he knows that there are not enough of them yet. For now, he is content just to plot with Walter, who lets him plunder some minor parts of the territory. But it won’t last: Brutus wants it all for himself and he sees Cat Tree City as a very juicy trophy.

Brutus makes the lives of the enslaved animals a living hell, and also for Jazzy the Yardogs’ Labrador blacksmith. In secret, Brutus also sells what he gets from looting to Walter (in exchange for treasure from the Great Pyramid) and helps maintain the reign of fear in the Kingdom of Cats.

This little game between Brutus and Walter would—if discovered—break the trust that the Yardogs have in their leader, and also put Walter in a difficult situation. Rumors say that Royal Guards have been seen trading with dogs at night at the gates of Cat Tree City, and that cat spies visit the Junkyard.

Brutus is an untidy individual, and a search of his apartment will reveal currency minted with Walter’s profile, as well as some compromising correspondence between the two plotters.

Strong 5 / Smart 5 / Cute 3 // Heart points 10 // Hiss & Growl; Knowledge of Laws & Legends; Scratch; Sweet-talk; Tinker with Bits & Bobs; // Fearless (1); Loud Speaker (1) // Large plate armor; thin but solid sword; a copy of Meowchiavelli’s book The Prince.

pages.name: p.128
pages.html:
Jazzy the blacksmith Jazzy the black Labrador is completely fed up with Brutus and his orders. For her, life is even harder since her best friend Luna was hounded out. She works her paws to the bone to forge armor, weapons, and shields for the Yardogs of the Junkyard. If they look so menacing, it’s mostly because of her! And she is grumpy, but that is mainly because she is so tired. She could be persuaded to side with the Kittens, or maybe even start a revolution against the Junkyard dogs, if the Kittens can earn her trust.

Strong 4 / Smart 3 / Cute 3 // Heart points 7 // Herbology; Keep Calm & Carry On; Tinker with Bits & Bobs // Safety at Work (1); Summon Tools (2) // Large leather apron; welding goggles; large hammer.

The Lovely Apollo Apollo the poodle never wished for this barbaric life. And although his childhood was very tough, he always saw beauty everywhere. His attitude is different from the other dogs in the pack. He is naturally calm and takes good care of his coat. He loves the arts and singing. As you would imagine, he is ignored by his peers. And although he dreams of a life elsewhere, his prospects seem limited.

Strong 1 / Smart 3 / Cute 5 // Heart points 4 // Keep Calm & Carry On; Make Music; Sweet-talk // Cat Haven (2); The Color of Grass (1) // Comb and brush; gloves.

Bish, Bash, and Bosh, the inseparable mutts These three hounds are Brutus’ most loyal allies. Their privileged status as second-incommands means they can bark at leisure at the workers, and spend their time bodybuilding by lifting heavy axles with tires at each end. They are not actually idiots—when taken individually—but once you put all three together it adds up to a huge helping of stupid.

Strong 5 / Smart 2 / Cute 3 // Heart points 7 // Hiss & Growl; Scratch // Fearless (1); Slipper Patrol (1) // Heavy armor; spikes; net for capturing creatures; strong rope.

pages.name: p.129 - Adventure trails To start with…
pages.html:
Adventure trails To start with…

The Kittens are captured during an am- bush and end up working in forced labor. Selene, the spirit of the Slumbering

Forest (see page 131) is unable to rest because of the noise and the heavy wood-burning for the forges. A friend of the Kittens has been captured by the Yardogs; they must get into the yard and release him (ideal for introducing a new Kitten to the group). The Kittens learn in Corktown that some

Yardogs from the Junkyard have settled close by and are causing trouble—and that’s not good for business. The cats of the Caravan Village have been forced to abandon their transport after an attack by the Yardogs. They have taken refuge at the edge of the Slumbering Forest. Without a roof over their heads, they are miserable and shivering. What can be done to get the caravans back before they are “repurposed” by the Yardogs? And maybe…

Jazzy the blacksmith is fed up with

Brutus’ impossible deadlines, so she starts thinking about overthrowing him. The Lovely Apollo causes a diversion by freeing the prisoners so he can take advantage of the chaos to escape from the Junkyard.

Bish, Bash, and Bosh have put together their three brain cells and realized that Brutus is not actually the strongest. On the other hand, as it is impossible that they will agree on who is the toughest of themselves, a fight is inevitable! And then…

Brutus finds some allies among the thugs who have joined up with Dark the goat (see page 163). Brutus forces his captured animals to explore Crimsonfief (see page 247) and bring back anything of value. If everything goes wrong for the Kittens

The Lovely Apollo will be able to try and free them to escape to Corktown and live the life of an artist. Jazzy will take over the Junkyard, chasing off Brutus and freeing the workers.

pages.name: p.131 - The Slumbering Forest
pages.html:
The Slumbering Forest

At the edge of the Kingdom of Cats and the Junkyard, lies an immense forest that is said to be meowgic. Until recently, it was home to animals who wanted to live in the wild, and others who wanted to be far from civilization. But since the Yardogs moved into the Junkyard with their mass felling of wood, many of those animals have preferred to flee. The heart of the forest has not moved: It is the domain of trees and Selene, who watches over her leafy group.

Selene is a spirit who takes the form of a huge owl with a plumage of leaves and two large horns made of flowering branches. Selene sleeps, lulled for a long time by the sound of the Dreamsinger (see page 155). The lifeforce of the woods flows from her enchanted dreams. She is a generous and peaceful spirit who welcomes exhausted travelers with kindness. Selene makes a springy moss grow beneath a camper’s bed and lulls them to sleep with the sound of a gentle fountain among the trees.

Unfortunately, as the years have passed, dogs, cats, and other animals have exploited the forest more and more.

Trees are chopped down to feed the Junkyard’s forges and to build the ever-increasing number of homes for cats. Selene’s lovely lullaby has gradually transformed to a stranger kind of music—the slow scraping of metal now fills the forest, waking the terrified creatures.

Selene, Spirit of the Forest

Selene is a huge meowgic owl, a creature born from the return of meowgic to the earth. She sleeps all the time, but her dreams come true in the real world. A double rainbow, a melodic waterfall, soft moss on a tree trunk that's more comfortable than a king’s throne: These are all little mirages that Selene is capable of, but if she has a nightmare, the worst abominations may come to life!

pages.name: p.132 - Adventure trails Forest’s edge
pages.html:
Luna the guardian This mysterious dog stands guard over Selene’s forest. She was actually born in the Junkyard, but she always hated Brutus' brutality. She fled and keeps on hoping that one day the Junkyard will be closed and the workers freed.

Strong 3 / Smart 4 / Cute 5 // Heart points 7 // Find Your Way; Heal Wounds & Diseases; Herbology; Hide in Shadows; See & Search; Shake Your Booty // Leather Apron (1); The Color of Grass (1) // A cape the color of the forest; a blacksmith's hammer.

Adventure trails Forest’s edge

Edmund (see Page 159) is determined to wreak havoc wherever he goes with the help of his cursed trumpet, Nightscreamer (see page 155), and his group, the Riders on the Storm. He plans to create an army of shadows, born from Selene’s nightmares. Dogs from the Junkyard roam the forest, cutting down trees for their forge and looking to kidnap stray animals to press into their workforce. The Caravan Village has settled on the edge of the forest, but between the Yardog attacks and the strange noises coming from the woods at night, they are not getting much peace.

In the forest

One day, the sun does not rise; the forest is plunged into darkness beneath a dome of purplish night from one of Selene’s nightmares. Her mind must be calmed so that the sun may once more return. Selene’s nightmares come to life in the form of creatures woven from the fabric of night, such as big black thorns or giant spiders with bodies covered in small, luminous stars. The forest awakens: the bushes growl like hibernating bears, the trees twist and bend with sinister creaking noises, the plants flower and then die at super-speed… something in the woods must be causing all these strange phenomena.

pages.name: p.134 - The Cricketers
pages.html:
The Cricketers

There is a strange brotherhood that lives on the edge of the Slumbering Forest. It is made up of cats and dogs who live together, bound by a strict code, their hatred of tyranny, and their love of freedom and speed: the Cricketers!

Recognizable from their thick leather vests that are decorated with (slightly scary!) studs and colorful patterns, the Cricketers have a very bad reputation. They are known as disrespectful brawlers, partyanimals, thieves, smugglers, and so on. Many of the crimes committed by Ptolemeow’s gang (see page 93) are blamed on them, and their wild appearance does not make people think any better of them.

The Cricketers is made up of cats who have left Cat Tree City and dogs who have abandoned the Junkyard and the tyranny of Brutus. They ride huge buzzing crickets, exoskeletons decorated with amazing paint jobs, and they tear around the countryside at breakneck speed—and are noisy as hell.

Anyone can become a Cricketer if they can pass the initiation test: Drink a lot, fight with the biggest member of the group, and—most important—catch your own cricket in the tall grass north of the forest. It is a very dangerous task: You have to find a cricket, catch it, mount it without being thrown off, and tame it until it bows to the paw of its new boss. All of this must be done without being eaten by the giant lizard that also lives in the grass (and has nothing against a change of diet—crickets at every meal is a bit dull).

pages.name: p.135
pages.html:
Buddy Buddy is the head of the Slumbering Forest’s chapter of Cricketers. He is a power ful cat, with broad, tattooed arms, thick fur, and drooping whiskers. He is the toughest and most relentless of the Cricketers, and he openly declares his opposition to both Walter and Brutus (for which the two tyrants have put a price on his head). Lately, however, Buddy has not been doing well and has been crying into his beer. It turns out that he fell in love with Luna but she sent him—and his cute little bouquet of rosehips—packing. His Cricketer pals have tried to cheer him up by taking him on more and more long, wild rides, but nothing helps. He is thinking of making his way to Corktown to drown his sorrows and then get on a ship bound for the other side of the world.

Strong 5 / Smart 3 / Cute 3 // Heart points 8 // Care of Beasts; Hiss & Growl; Scratch; Shake Your Booty; Sweet-talk // Blessing of Honor (1); Long Night (3); Sense Trouble (3) // A cricket called Daytona; a leather jacket with badges on it; a bandana with skulls; a long, metal chain.

Adventure trails The Kittens camp south of Huggle in an old ship graveyard when they hear the strange noise of a giant cricket. It stops at the old, ruined lighthouse on the rocky peninsula. It is Buddy, who is all by himself. He has come to get drunk before he makes his way to Corktown. But he has been followed by some Yardogs, who beat him up, damaged his cricket, and even tried to throw him over the cliff. What can be done with this big wounded cat, who is silent, humiliated, sobbing, and who refuses to talk about his problems? Luna hates big lunks, wherever they are from. How do you prove to her that Buddy really has a big heart?

pages.name: p.137 - The Witch’s Lair
pages.html:
The Witch’s Lair

In the heart of a small, sparse forest, behind some huge, rusted gates, at the end of an overgrown path, hides the Lair of Suzanne, the witch viper. This disturbing reptile lives in a ruined tower—in truth, a former pigeon loft—on the edge of a pond filled with water lilies. There is a big, old boat in the pond that looks like a ghost ship—an old fisherman’s boat—which serves as a rest point for the many birds that pass this way.

Suzanne has an amazing gift that means countless rumors are told about her: she is psychic! She can predict the future and gives enigmatic prophecies—this is why she is known as a witch. In payment for a vision, Suzanne asks for a ring of precious metal. She has used the treasure she has accumulated over the years to make beautiful ornaments that she curls up in.

Many animals make a pilgrimage to visit the viperwitch. They face up to any fears they may have in order to learn more about the world’s mysteries. And Suzanne takes her role very seriously. Contrary to what is said about her, and what her cold and haughty attitude may indicate, Suzanne is committed to helping those around her.

Over the years, several animals have been so impressed by the unique gift of the viper that they have entered her service.

Cheddar George, an old muskrat, proclaimed himself head of Suzanne’s guard, although he is still its only member. Lady Sibyl, a magpie, is the estate’s housekeeper—she welcomes visitors and carefully manages the affairs of her ladyboss; and while Suzanne keeps her distance from real-world concerns, the magpie is a pragmatic creature, although she does suffer from a little lack of recognition. Finally, twin chatty moorhens, Marikatolsn and Ashliolsn, take care of the daily chores and try to keep the tower in good order.

But the sinister Bojosar has his sights set on this sacred domain. This big cane toad is a horrible, poisonous, cunning brute. He sits on a throne of junk that is carried by his toad henchmen, and he constantly talks of his own legend. It is the story of a sovereign unjustly cast out because he was just too kind—a wandering king in search of a new domain that is worthy of welcoming him. As you can guess, this is obviously not the reality! Bojosar likes to attract the sympathy and loyalty of animals he meets by giving out food and stolen coins. Bit by bit, thanks to this divisive, selfish method, he has managed to gather a big bunch of bullies around him. And now that he has the means, he intends to invade Suzanne’s home and drive her out—unless he decides to make her his personal prophetess? The enormous toad wants to impose his law on the whole region: His ambition matches his impressive physique and his endless appetite.

pages.name: p.138 - Suzanne, the witch viper
pages.html:
Bojosar's plan Here are the steps in his plan to take over Suzanne’s land:

1. Order his group to wander discreetly around, to spy on these places: the forest, the pond’s surroundings, the pond, and finally the foot of the tower—where the adventure begins! 2. Turn up at the pond under a false, friendly pretext, then later intimidate and threaten Suzanne and her family. 3. If the inhabitants resist (and they will), conduct a ruthless attack to take over the former pigeon loft—first by threats and intimidation, then perhaps by using more brutal and bloody methods. 4. Capture the viper or enslave her. The unexpected arrival of the Kittens will be good for Suzanne, because the heroes could get involved in this miserable affair.

Suzanne, the witch viper

A distant reptile who always seems to be far from this world.

Strong 4 / Smart 5 / Cute 3 // Heart points 9 // Herbology; Keep Calm & Carry On; Knowledge of Laws & Legends; Seduce & Charm // Enchanting Voice (2); Loud Speaker (1); Sense Trouble (3); Talk to Trees (3); Words of Wisdom (2).

pages.name: p.139 - Cheddar George,
pages.html:
Cheddar George,

his own boss A brave old muskrat, getting on a bit. Strong 3 / Smart 3 / Cute 2 // Heart points 6 // Find Information; Hiss & Growl; Scratch; See & Search // Cat’s Eyes (1); Fearless (1) // A halberd; a blue military helmet.

Lady Sibyl, housekeeper

A well-organized magpie, overworked and underappreciated.

Strong 2 / Smart 3 / Cute 3 // Heart points 5 // Cook; Knowledge of Laws & Legends; Read, Write, Count // Clean & Tidy (1); Preserving Resources (1) // A notebook and a mechanical pencil; a white apron.

Marikatolsn and

Ashliolsn Two talkative, clumsy water hens (difficult to tell them apart).

Strong 3 / Smart 1 / Cute 2 // Heart points 4 // Care of Beasts; Cook; Shake Your Booty; Hunter-Gatherer // Blessing of Honor (1); Treating Beasts (1) // A small kitchen knife; a bag to put things in; a colorful blouse decorated with flowers and nice little patterns.

Bojosar A huge, lying, nasty, unpleasant cane toad. Strong 5 / Smart 4 / Cute 3 // Heart points 9 // Hiss & Growl; Knowledge of Laws & Legends; Pickpocket; Scratch; Seduce & Charm; Shake Your Booty; Sweet-talk // Endless Feed (2); Loud Speaker (1) // A gold ring.

pages.name: p.140 - Adventure trails To start with…
pages.html:
Robber toads A band of ugly, dumb scoundrels. Strong 3 / Smart 1 / Cute 2 // Heart points 4 // Hiss & Growl; Shake Your Booty // Slipper Patrol (1); The Color of Grass (1) // A heavy wooden flask.

Adventure trails To start with…

The Kittens get caught in a thunderstorm.

After a stressful journey in the forest —large rusting, creaky gates, a pond where moonlight is reflected perfectly despite the rain, sinister shadows, and so on—, they find refuge with the slightly disturbing Suzanne, who turns out to be more welcoming than you might think.

The Kittens have heard about the witch viper and decide to consult her to find out more about their exile. But do they have the means to pay for a vision? Where will they find a precious ring? The Kittens spot the robber toads—they even hear them boasting about their planned invasion of the pond. True heroes can't stand idly by! The Kittens flee when they are attacked by the Yardogs from the Junkyard (see page 125). They get lost in the woods near the pond. Mama, from the Caravan Village (see page 111), tells of the amazing powers of Suzanne the seer in front of the Kittens.

pages.name: p.141
pages.html:
And maybe…

Lady Sibyl betrays her boss and joins the horrible Bojosar who, despite his brutal demeanour, has a certain charm… and in particular a thirst for power and wealth that could attract the magpie. The bird is tired of doing everything while her boss remains aloof and ungrateful for her efforts. The big, wooden ship contains some mysterious treasure: Odd little shiny fish, carved from unknown gems. Surely they are worth a fortune (in fact, they are plastic fishing floats made with glitter). Mogg the toad, one of Bojosar’s hench- men, refuses to attack the viper. He has realized the true nature of his boss, and he could be of help to the heroes. And then…

Once Suzanne is rescued, perhaps other animals could be convinced to help her, in order to avoid another invasion? The baron of the nearby city of Corktown (see page 143) may be able to do somethingwith skilled negotiation. What will the psychic reveal to the characters? What is the meaning of her strange vision, where a door locks shut, and a huge, shining, metal wheel is found? (see Bigwheel, page 155)?

What is this sinister, windswept spot at the edge of the ocean?! (see Crimsonfief, page 247). If he is defeated, will Bojosar flee, only to return with reinforcements? Will he go so far as to forge a terrifying pact with Dark (see page 163), or will he pay Brutus and the Yardogs to set Suzanne’s home on fire (see page 125)?

pages.name: p.143 - Corktown, city of a thousand taverns
pages.html:
Corktown, city of a thousand taverns

At the end of a rocky peninsula, on the edge of the known world, stands a stunning city. Beaten by wind, waves, and spray, the port is protected from nature and invasion by a massive wall. The name of this place? Corktown.

It is overcrowded, dirty, smelly, and full of narrow passages. But it is also cosmopolitan, exotic, and liberal. The city welcomes everything that the sea washes in, including sailors and scoundrels alike. One-eyed parrots, tattooed, muscular crabs, and fish in diving suits all mix freely. This motley crew of old seadogs has been around the world in all sorts of ships, from fast-paced frigates to leaky old tankers. There are traders, pirates, explorers—even simple ships’ stokers. This fellowship of the sea embodies a spirit of freedom that has long been missing from the Kingdom of Cats, and its seafaring members bring swashbuckling stories and marvellous merchandise to Corktown.

The flourishing port of Corktown, safe behind its city wall, has evolved over time into a maze like collection of jetties and quays. Ships of all sizes, merchants, fishermen, and pirates anchor here all year round. The city is a buzzing hive of commerce where anything can be bought and sold.

Corktown is also famous for its countless drinking dens and typical barrel-shaped buildings. The many inns and taverns that line the streets are open day and night. Wild nights out here are legendary. The beer flows freely. The festive atmosphere attracts seafarers and landlubbers alike. Some of the more famous establishments include The Pink Seagull, The Apple in the Mouth, The Happy Hog, and The Bar at the End of the World.

pages.name: p.144 - The Rinswith-Gutrotters
pages.html:
The Rinswith-Gutrotters

In this city, law and order are loose concepts. Here in Corktown it is the strongest, the richest, or the loudest who win. This anarchical atmosphere attracts plenty of people in search of a dark corner where they can conduct their shady business, as well as those who want to disappear.

And at the top of the pile of these stinking sea-crates is one family: the Rinswith-Gutrotters. This extensive tribe of pigs comprises a huge number of brothers, sisters, uncles, aunts, nephews, cousins, and in-laws. In every one of the city’s many inns and taverns there is a Rinswith-Gutrotter, either serving behind the bar themselves or paying one of their trusted followers to do it.

At the top of the lot sits the Baron, the most powerful Rinswith-Gutrotter, who made it to the top and stays there through cunning and swordsmanship. At present, it is the excruciating Embergrunt who has just taken over, following the recent death of his uncle. This spotted swine is now in charge of the whole family.

However, although the presence of the Rinswith-Gutrotters is everywhere, they are not as intrusive and tyrannical as the fat Walter. As long as nobody meddles in their business, they quietly ignore the other inhabitants of the city and argue only with each other.

pages.name: p.145 - Neighborhoods
pages.html:
And should anyone so much as touche a hair on the snout of any of them, the whole family unites against that unlucky creature.

Iron Loins The Iron Loins are the elite militia of the Rinswith-Gutrotters. They watch the city gates and patrol the streets. These henchmen rule by force and obey only the orders of the Baron. Their task is not to keep law and order (there isn’t any!), but only to look after the interests of the Rinswith-Gutrotters.

Neighborhoods

Corktown is a colorful place with many possibilities for adventure for a group of brave Kittens. Here are the main neighborhoods:

The Wall and the Salt Gate

Corktown is protected by an imposing wall, made up of all sorts of materials. It is visible from a long way away, whether you arrive by road or by sea. It is made of wood and stone, as well as remnants of the olden days: tires, car wrecks, reinforced concrete blocks, barbed wire, and so on. The path that leads to the end of the peninsula and into the city ends at a vast archway that is sealed by a heavy, rusty portcullis: the Salt Gate. This entrance is always guarded by the Iron Loins.

Notable places The Pork Fortress, the Iron Loins’ impressive barracks. The Stripy Tower, a wobbly watchtower from where all the surrounding area can be observed. It is an old red and white radio mast. Mrs. Cuddles’ Dispensary is a make- shift building made of old riveted sheet metal, leaning against the Wall.

pages.name: p.146 - The Hook
pages.html:
The Hook

Behind the Wall, the dilapidated, squalid, poor quarter splays out. This is where the city's workers live: Waiters, servants, brewery workers, fishermen, fishmongers… it is filthy. It is not a good place to hang around at night, with a high risk of being robbed by a local gang such as the cunning Maggots or the brutal Red Hooks.

Notable places The Daedalus district is, a dangerous wasteland, full of holes and cracks. Better Here Than There! is, the city’s shabbiest inn, directly opposite the Daedalus district. This establishment is run by Plonky, a skunk with a bad temper. The poorest families are crammed into

The Shack, the biggest and most run-down building in the neighborhood.

The Porkery

All the Rinswith-Gutrotters, along with the other wealthy members of the city, live in the center of Corktown, above the harbor district. The Porkery is a haven of luxury that contrasts sharply with the neighborhood (although the cleanliness of Corktown always leaves something to be desired).

Notable places The Baron’s Palace, the richest and

most impressive building of the city (but is decorated in utterly bad taste). The Muddy Gardens, a park of ploughed land that is copiously watered each morning by a horde of servants in stained uniforms. It is a very popular place for the Rinswith-Gutrotters to (st)roll around. The Golden Slipper Resort Hotel is the most unique, prestigious inn in the Porkery. It is owned by the enormous Teppid, the angry younger brother of Baron Embergrunt.

pages.name: p.147 - Land’s End Port
pages.html:
Land’s End Port

Further down towards the sea is Land’s End, the harbor district. It is the largest neighborhood in Corktown. And it stinks! It smells of a mixture of seaweed, alcohol, and fish. Land’s End is filled with breweries, distilleries, marine warehouses, fish shops, docks, a shipyard, the harbor master’s office, and a number of stores selling nautical, fishing, or travel equipment. Land’s End is even more chaotic than the rest of the city. Barrel-shaped buildings and gigantic pipes from stills make getting around difficult and unpredictable. There’s hardly enough room to swing a cat! There are also more hostels and taverns here than anywhere else.

Notable places The White Whale, a store run by

Ahab, a bad-tempered old bear who is a former guard from a faraway city. He now sells the best nets and harpoons. The Compass Rose, a shop selling maps, sextants, and spy glasses. It is said that the boss, Charby the dolphin, sells treasure maps in exchange for a share of the loot.

The Harbor-master’s Office is where

the albino pig, Rik Rinswith Gutrotter, collects taxes and organizes arrivals and departures as best he can. The brewery of the venerable Qwak

Rinswith-Gutrotter—a beer factory. (Think oil refinery, but with hops!) Some famous ships and their illustrious captains

The Turtle, a huge freight transport boat that makes its way from port to port. The albatross captain, Jo, is an old sea dog who knows the coast like the back of his claw. The Stormy, a shiny pirate ship, is sleek and fast. The crew are famous—and frightening. They are totally devoted to their sea-otter captain, the fearsome Cap’Orn. The Phantom is a small smuggler’s ship with a dark hull. Its captain, a one-eyed dog named Dutch, is a rogue and a thief. But if you want to travel discreetly or transport shady goods, he is your man.

pages.name: p.148
pages.html:
Encounters Baron Embergrunt Embergrunt is a spotted pig who does not look like much. He is seen as skinny compared to the rest of his family, but his intelligence and cruelty are second to none. Even pirate captains or the fiercest ship bosses are scared of him! But all this, despite everything, is just for show—to keep his family calm and scare the competition. In fact, in private, he is quite kind and he has some grand plans for his city and its inhabitants. If only his cousins and brothers were not such idiots! He could do with the help of some strong, smart, and cute allies.

Strong 1 / Smart 5 / Cute 5 // Heart points 6 // Find Information; Keep Calm & Carry On; Seduce & Charm;

Sweet-talk // Enchanting

Voice (2); Sense

Trouble (3) // A baron’s crown; a thin stylus hidden in his boots; various antidotes against all kinds of poison.

A typical Iron Loin The Iron Loins are a bunch of mercenaries who make up the Rinswith-Gutrotters’ militia. They patrol the city with iron trotters and look after the interests of the Rinswith-Gutrotters. They are mean, ugly, stupid, and well-armed!

Strong 4 / Smart 2 / Cute 2 // Heart points 6 // Hiss & Growl; Shake Your Booty // Fearless (1); Loud Speaker (1) // A helmet; armor; and a pike.

pages.name: p.149
pages.html:
A typical local rogue Corktown has a huge collection of thugs of all kinds—and species. And whether they are Maggots or Red Hooks, they tend to frequent taverns, dark alleys, and crowded markets… in short, they are everywhere. Don't look for trouble and hold on to your purse!

Strong 3 / Smart 2 / Cute 1 // Heart points 5 // Hide in Shadows; Move Silently; Pickpocket // A hood that smells fishy.

A typical sailor/pirate It is easy to recognize a sailor. They always like to talk. They often wear baggy pants, a bandana or a hat, and they usually have some body part missing (replaced with an eye patch, a hook, or a wooden leg). There is also a strange odor: a sickening mix of sea, sardines, and sweat. But the sign you can never mistake is the spark in the eye when they talk about their latest adventure at sea…

Strong 4 / Smart 3 / Cute 1 // Heart points 7 // Read Sky & Stars; Shake Your Booty // Breathe Under water (1); Long View (2) // A meerschaum pipe; a compass.

Mrs. Cuddles This white cat with a big heart is a survivor, in her own way. Her husband and seven sons went out to sea one day... and never came back. But she has never given up hope of hearing from them again. In the meantime, she runs a dispensary with what few resources she manages to get hold of, in order to provide shelter and care to the most needy, who she treats like her own children.

Strong 1 / Smart 3 / Cute 4 // Heart points 4 // Cook; Heal Wounds & Diseases; Herbology // Care (3); Heart Charm (1) // Large kitchen apron; ladle.

pages.name: p.150 - Adventure trails To start with…
pages.html:
Ahoy there mateys! As you can see, there are no specific rules for ships and navigation. There are no specific skills for this either. The stories in Dungeons and Kittens usually take place on dry land, but if your Kittens take to water for an adventure, here are some tips:

Most of the actions that can be done on a boat (steering, hoisting the mainsail, loading cannons, etcetera) can use Shake Your Booty. Actions that are specific to navigation (plotting a course, avoiding reefs, catching the wind) can use Read Sky & Stars. Journeys by ship—and the adventures that happen there, including being boarded—are treated as if they were on land. Above all, Kittens should avoid falling into the water! Generally speaking, unless the adventure specifically mentions it, ships do not sink easily when Kittens are on board!

Adventure trails To start with…

After rescuing Suzanne the viper witch, the Kittens arrive in Corktown to try and get help to protect her pond sanctuary in future. To speed up the journey, the Kittens take a ship from Huggle (see page 115) to the north-east of Cat Tree City. They land at Corktown and discover the city of the Rinswith-Gutrotters. The Kittens heard about Corktown during a stop at an inn on the way. It sounds as if it is an absolute must-see! You can board a ship from there to travel even farther afield.

pages.name: p.151
pages.html:
The Kittens could be fleeing from the Black Horns, the army of Dark (see page 160), and wind up hiding in Corktown. The Kittens arrive in Corktown with the cats from the Caravan Village, but chances are the Yardogs from the Junkyard are not far behind.

And maybe…

Mrs. Cuddles’ dispensary is under threat from the Red Hooks gang (see page 146). Their leader, Gizzard the lizard, wants to take the place over for his own ends. And despite the requests of the caring cat for protection, the Baron seems to take no interest in the story. The population of the Hook are too frightened to do anything. Without help, what will become of the refuge of the downtrodden? Part of the Wall has collapsed. The au- thorities are looking for material to re-build it. It seems that there is quite a lot that’s suitable in the bay: The sea floor is littered with usable objects from the olden days. To use it, you would need to make an agreement with the fish that live down there. Unfortunately, they are not too keen on the Baron since their leader, Aynt, had an argument with him about yet another fishing tax. But brilliant negotiators could pull off a deal!

It seems that inhabitants of the Shack have been disappearing mysteriously at night. The population of the Hook are frightened, but the Iron Loins don’t care (see page 148). Herman, the old tomcat from the top floor, is willing to pay for clever investigators to look into the matter. Some fear that a band of rat kidnappers have settled in the middle of the Daedalus district. And while we’re at it, where did Herman’s fortune come from? Zaza, the Rinswith-Gutrotter owner of The Pink Seagull has organized a masquerade! She is offering full board and lodging for a whole week to the winners. Kittens will need to travel all over the city to find original accessories: sparkling scales from the port, little bits from the Wall (see page 145), rolls of precious fabric from the Porkery, not to mention the know-how of Kal, the best sail sewer from the Hook… What a great opportunity to visit the whole city!

pages.name: p.152
pages.html:
Captain Dutch, the owner of The Phantom, is up to something. He’s been seen hanging out at night on the docks with a lantern in his hand as if he were waiting for someone. Could it be that he’s smuggling something new into the city or that he’s waiting to transport a fugitive? It is said that he does business with the Black Horns. It is also said that beer has been disappearing from the cellars of certain inns and taverns— and that he is behind it. Charby, the dolphin owner of the Compass

Rose (see page 147), is in panic. Ever since he came into possession of a strange map, his nights have been troubled. It seems like a ghost is haunting his shop after midnight. The dolphin is looking for some heroes to protect him and possibly give the map back to Cap’Orn (see page 147), who he bought it from. What if the pirate otter is playing Charby, and he’s the one behind the whole charade? Investigating and getting on board The Stormy will require Kittens to be careful and courageous.

And then…

It seems like a strange prophetess has settled in a forest not far from a pond (see page 137). It is said that she will predict the future in exchange for a precious ring. Fortunately, Teppid—owner of the The Golden Slipper Resort Hotel (see page 146)—is offering a golden ring to any group of hard workers who can help him organize a birthday party for the Baron, his brother.

Along the coast, you can land at the foot of Crimsonfief (see page 247); in the olden days this was a castle, but today it is a ruin. It is said that Crimsonfief contains great treasures, but many who have risked a journey there have never returned… To the east stands Bigwheel, a magical, wonderful place (see page 155). Appa rently it is a crazy fun place to visit. Kittens will certainly want to go there and have a look around. Another village has been attacked! The

Kittens meet some fugitives on the road to Corktown. These refugees tell of soldiers who carry a banner with two black horns on it (see page 163). Pokkay, the crab captain of The Scoffer, a deep-sea fishing boat, discovered a strange island made of metal (see page 175). After a terrible storm, his ship found itself at the foot of some huge iron pillars that keep the island above the water. Pokkay is not keen to go back and explore this unknown territory, even though it must be full of hidden treasure. A “big-bare-butt” was spotted not far from

Corktown. Baron Embergrunt is looking for brave adventurers to go and confirm if this is true or not. He doesn't want to risk his precious Iron Loins (see page 148)! In exchange, he will be willing to hear out any grievances or requests for rewards. The giant may have been spotted near the hills along the Cheeki river (see page 168).

pages.name: p.155
pages.html:
Bigwheel, land of laughter and dreams Dualeaper the raccoon chose to always look on the bright side of life. He had enough of the hassle and bickering of his busy family, so left everything to pursue a carefree life of laughter. After wandering around for a while, he met up with Ernest the master bear, and his troop of acrobats, the Rainbow Tumble Tribe. In their company, going from farm to village and through the few cities of the region, Dualeaper learned many trades: storyteller, singer, entertainer, acrobat, clown. He quickly became hugely popular with both the public and his comrades. And wherever Dualeaper put on a show, happiness seemed to follow!

Impressed by his talent, old Ernest declared Dualeaper his heir and trusted him enough to take over the Rainbow Tumble Tribe. Above all, he gave the raccoon his greatest treasure: a strange and wonderful set of magic bagpipes named Dreamsinger.

“This instrument has been passed from paw to paw for countless generations,” he told young Dualeaper. Its origin dates back to the time when the first animals were gifted with speech, when the first two students of the very first archmeowge—who were jealous of each other—created two magical instruments: Dreamsinger, a set of bagpipes, and NIghtscreamer, a trumpet. It is not known what happened to the two apprentice meowges, but their instruments fell into the hands of two groups of competing acrobats: the Rainbow Tumble Tribe and the Riders on the Storm. “The power you now hold in your hands,” continued the old bear, “can affect people’s dreams, can give them the best night’s sleep, can heal their ailments, and sooth their anxieties.”

Dualeaper and the Rainbow Tumble Tribe continued to travel around the country for a long time. Often they found themselves caught up in the old quarrel with the Riders on the Storm. And then Dualeaper, by then a little old and a little ill, found an opportunity. Dualeaper bought the distant ruins of an amusement park of the olden days from Baron Embergrunt of Corktown. With hard work and determination, the place was gradually rebuilt. The raccoon has made it an enclave of freedom, dedicated to entertainment.

pages.name: p.156
pages.html:
Dualeaper’s crowning achievement was to restore the great Ferris wheel that stands in the middle of the complex. And these days the entire park is named after that huge wheel.

There, protected from the aggression of the Riders on the Storm, Dualeaper welcomes people who need to recharge their batteries and forget their troubles, like the misery and sorrow of everyday life, or the anxiety caused by a dangerous world that’s ruled by tyrants and brigands. The joy of a carefree moment and the happiness of laughter, can, according to him, prevent animals from falling into the ancient patterns of human misery: jealousy, wickedness, greed, and pettiness.

Balladeers, minstrels, troubadours, street artists, and circus artists are found all year-round in Bigwheel and there are fabulous shows. Some animals live there permanently— especially ageing artists for whom traveling is difficult—and a small band of artisans and merchants have taken refuge there and help Dualeaper out where they can.

The amusement park remains mostly deserted. Travelling artists talk about it wherever they go, fuelling the hopes and dreams of the people they visit. It has become the subject of many conversations, but very few animals will brave the roads to get there: Between the tyrannical powers that are found everywhere and the fear of brigands and monsters, most people are too scared to venture far from home, unless they can get safe passage with a caravan.

Dualeaper knows that people will come one day—maybe when all the bad guys in the world have finally been defeated and people can live in peace. Bigwheel is a beacon in the darkness, representing this hope. The brighter the park’s light, the quicker the tyrants will be brought down!

pages.name: p.157
pages.html:
Encounters Dualeaper Dualeaper is always cheerful, singing, and jumping (although he does suffer from terrible bouts of gout). Nothing surprises him and he always has a good joke up his sleeve. Although he is usually busy with his work, he still tries to make time to enjoy the park, joking with visitors, making children laugh, and having fun on the rides. He is instantly recognizable with his clown suit and big red shoes, a squirting flower, and a large top hat. He frequently bursts into applause, clapping his paws together at the slightest opportunity. Dualeaper has learned to play Dreamsinger perfectly and will use it on visitors who ask him.

Strong 2 // Smart 5 // Cute 5 // Heart points 7 // Draw & Paint; Knowledge of People & Places; Make Music; Seduce & Charm; Shake Your Booty // Backpack: Strange bagpipes.

Rainbow Tumble Tribe The Rainbow Tumble Tribe is made up of good-natured, cheerful, and friendly creatures. There are about thirty members, comprising pretty much all species with the gift of speech. They are dressed in harlequin costumes covered in diamonds of all the colors of the rainbow, with a half-moon hat and a black eye mask. It’s what they used to wear on stage, when they were still traveling from village to village. Today it is their uniform in their role as Bigwheel’s friendly guards. They faithfully serve Dualeaper, the bearer of Dreamsinger.

Strong 3 / Smart 2 / Cute 3 // Heart points 5 // Make Music; Shake Your Booty // Juggling balls and clubs; ribbons and scarves.

pages.name: p.159 - The Riders on the Storm
pages.html:
Edmund Edmund is a turtle with a dark shell and red-and-brown mottled skin. He is always dressed in a dark red cape. From his position in the sedan chair that he never leaves, he spits out his orders to his followers, the Riders on the Storm. He is the bearer of the trumpet Nightscreamer, which he plays with extraordinary brilliance and mastery. He is nevertheless sad hateful, and angry. He does not understand why Dualeaper always tries to avoid the fighting that makes life worth living, which is part of an ancient tradition that must be respected no matter what. In the meantime, he rents out the use of his trumpet to anyone who wishes to inflict disturbing nights on their enemies.

Strong 4 / Smart 4 / Cute 4 // Heart points 8 // Herbology; Hiss & Growl; Make Music; Knowledge of Laws & Legends; Seduce & Charm // Animate Object (3); Feel the Path (3) // A beautiful silver trumpet; a long, dark red cape.

The Riders on the Storm

The Riders on the Storm are an angry, boastful bunch of creatures. There are about thirty of them, including nearly every species that can talk. They dress all in black, including their masks and hats, and each carries a rapier by their side. They are superb performers, acrobats, and pranksters. Although they are constantly insulted and humiliated by Edmund, they serve the old turtle with loyalty that borders on fanaticism.

Strong 3 / Smart 3 / Cute 2 // Heart points 6 // Hide in Shadows; Shake Your Booty // Wooden rapier; black mask.

pages.name: p.160 - Adventure trails To start with…
pages.html:
Adventure trails To start with…

The Kittens have heard about Bigwheel and are curious. They want to discover this fabulous place. The Kittens have a strange, recurring dream. They travel to consult the guardian of the Dreamsinger to find out what it could mean. Here is a list of strange, recurring dreams for the Kittens, which could encourage them to visit Bigwheel: A Kitten dreams that he becomes king instead of Walter; dreams he is flying around with an old owl; dreams that he is a fish swimming around the keels of ships; dreams that he is invisible; dreams that he writes a neverending story; or dreams that an angry, fuming black goat chases and tries to trap him… The Kittens escort a convoy that is delivering a cargo of sugar and cocoa to Bigwheel. It is a very significant delivery, for the merchants and Bigwheel, but robbers (or Dark’s Black Horn horde, see page 166) are lurking.

And maybe…

Suzanne the witch-viper has a terrible nightmare: Bigwheel was attacked by a sombre trumpet player accompanied by a troop of sinister swordsmen. She asks the valiant heroes who have already saved her from Bojosar’s slime (see page 137) to help prevent the destruction of the kingdom of happiness and laughter. Dark’s troops are marching for Corktown, and Bigwheel is on the way. Dualeaper has no idea that the Black Horns are approaching, so the Kittens will have to warn him. And then, maybe Dreamsinger can help reconcile the goat with his true story and identity, so he may finally go back to being Horn (see page 163).

pages.name: p.161
pages.html:
And then…

Dualeaper could ask the Kittens to go on a shopping trip for him in Corktown. The raccoon cannot stand to visit the city that’s teeming with bad sorts. He might ask them to look in at The Pink Seagull to see if Mrs. Zaza has some new performers to show them. The Kittens meet Godfrey, a wild boar looking for treasure. He is the last survivor of an expedition to the depths of Crimsonfief that went badly wrong. The boar is terribly upset and he has come to recover in Bigwheel. Eventually, after sharing a thousand stories with them, he gives the group a scribbled map of the dungeon. Victor the rabbit is on his way to

Suzanne the viper-witch’s hideout. He is looking for brave adventurers to accompany him. He heard that some henchmen were prowling around (Black Horns). A hare cousin of his even told him that a big, sneaky toad has been seen in the area.

pages.name: p.163 - Misty Valley
pages.html:
Misty Valley

Misty Valley is a steep valley through which the Cheeki river runs. In the middle is an aged dam from the olden days—every morning, mist rises from the dam’s lake and disappears in the midday sun. This is where the Black Horns are camped out with their leader, the sinister Dark.

Dark

Hear ye, hear ye, listen to the sad and terrible story of Dark, the sheep who wasn’t a sheep. Mrs. Bloomunday, a lady sheep of good stock, with soft wool, one day gave birth to a lamb with a coat as dark as coal, who was smaller than his brothers and sisters and also more disruptive. He developed strangely, grew a goatee, small horns, and had a strange look in his eye. Even his dad, Mr. Bloomunday, who loved him very much (and loved his wife very much), found him a bit odd. Everyone called the young sheep Horn and he became the laughing stock of the area. At home, things went from bad to worse: His parents kept arguing, and his sisters and brothers bullied and laughed at him.

Horn decided to leave, thinking everything would work out better if he went. Wandering the highways in search of his identity and a future, he came across Casper, a cunning and very wise fox.
